back: An event, measurable in money, that changes the financial position of a business (a sale, purchase, payment or receipt).
The detailed, day-to-day recording of financial transactions.
Summarising the records into financial statements, then analysing and interpreting them for decision-making.
Assets kept for more than a year to run the business, not for resale (premises, machinery, vehicles, fittings).
Cash, or items expected to become cash within a year: inventory, trade receivables, bank, cash.
Amounts owed and due within twelve months: trade payables, bank overdraft, expenses owing.
Money, goods or other assets taken from the business by the owner for personal use. They reduce capital, not profit.

front: Is a loan repayment an expense?
back: No. It reduces a liability. Only the interest on the loan is an expense.

front: Is a bank overdraft an asset or a liability?
back: A current liability: money owed to the bank and repayable on demand.

front: Why can the same vehicle be classified differently in two businesses?
back: Classification depends on purpose: held for resale it is inventory (current); used to run the business it is a non-current asset.
